title: Embrace spooky season with paranormal romance books by a Tampa Bay author

content:
Tampa Bay overflows with talented authors, and in August, FloridaRAMA hosted its first-ever LitFest, a celebration of Tampa Bay's vibrant literary community, with 30 local writers. Enjoy some of their interviews in future columns and online: bit.ly/3Jx1mla

Haunted romance

Local author Tamara Lush, who also writes under her pen name, Tara Lush, has two new paranormal romance books out just in time for scary season. "A Spell for Second Chances," a spinoff of her "Crescent Moon" series, comes out Sept. 18. Think forest magic, fall pumpkin festivals, a talking moose and a murder set against the backdrop of Hemlock Hollow, Vermont. Said Lush: "If you've read my 'Crescent Moon' books, you'll love this (and will recognize a familiar character). 'The Paradise Wish,' book five and the final story in the 'Starlight River Cozy Romance' series, is out as well, closing out Cypress Grove's most romantically complicated family."

Here's what "The Paradise Wish" is about: Natalia Hastings is the only single Hastings sibling in Cypress Grove — the self-proclaimed "Psychic Capital of the World" — and she'd like everyone to stop making a big deal about it. Designing one-of-a-kind necklaces, helping her brother Max run the Magnolia Grande and dodging dating app weirdos is more than enough. Then the Visitors Bureau pairs her with Matthew Mancini, a charming, divorced single dad and brand-new helicopter pilot, who is in town for a photo shoot at the springs. By sunset, the camera has captured something neither of them was planning to let anyone see: attraction.

It might be the easiest love story in Cypress Grove history. Until Mancini's family arrives in town for the weekend, and Hastings recognizes a face she's spent 15 years pretending she doesn't remember. Now she's forced to make a choice between her past and present, and she's not sure if all the magic in Cypress Grove will help. taralush.com

Book clubs/events

Oxford Exchange: Two of Oxford Exchange's monthly book clubs are at St. Pete's The Library restaurant at lunchtime and 6 p.m. Plus, on Sept. 28, it will hold a midnight release party for Rebecca Yarros' highly anticipated "Threshing Day" short story collection, where you can enjoy refreshments, literary games and more. Costumes are encouraged for guests.

Gridiron fans will enjoy Oxford Exchange's Sept. 30 conversation with Greg Auman and New York Times bestselling author Lars Anderson about his new book, "Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness." oxfordexchange.com

Arts Passport Book Club: Tampa Bay Arts Passport is the brainchild of founder Avery Anderson. On Sept. 27 at 3 p.m., the organization's Arts Passport Book Club will talk about Janice Hadlow's "The Other Bennet Sister" followed by a private 6 p.m. showing of "Jane Austen in 89 Minutes" at Tampa's Stageworks Theatre. The book club offers members a chance to explore literature that connects with upcoming plays, art shows or exhibitions in collaboration with Tombolo Books. tbartspassport.com/book-club

Storytelling Amateur Hour: Purpose-Driven Professionals and Book + Bottle are collaborating on a new low-pressure open mic event on the first Wednesday of every month from 6-8 p.m. Your words don't have to be polished, perfected or rehearsed. Poetry and short stories are welcome. Or you can read a favorite children's story or a short story by a favorite author. Readers will have five minutes at the mic. The sign-up sheet goes live at 6 p.m.; stories start at 6:30 p.m. bookandbottlestpete.com/events

Fenway Hotel: In addition to fabulous food, jazz and perhaps the best sunset view in Tampa Bay from its rooftop bar, this Dunedin hot spot has a free monthly book club on select Tuesdays at 7 p.m. Guests are encouraged to read the selected book in advance and RSVP ahead of time and can receive 20% off the featured book at Back in the Day Books in downtown Dunedin. fenwayhotel.com
